paragraphs.text: A [Taiwan oolong](taiwan-oolong:definition) from Beipu, in Hsinchu County, made in 1970 with a medium roast and packed in tea bags. Hsinchu is one of the two counties where the island makes Oriental Beauty, though this tea is a roasted oolong of the area.

Fifty-six years on, it is well past the ten to thirty years that those who give a figure count as old, which puts it among Taiwan's [lao cha](taiwan-oolong:ageing), old tea. Oolong kept this way starts well roasted and dry, because moisture is what the years have to be kept from. Cool, dark, sealed storage, and a low roast now and then to drive moisture out, are how an old oolong is looked after.

brewing.text: Ball-rolled Taiwan oolong takes hot water, about 90 to 100°C, a fairly generous amount of leaf and short steeps; the balls open slowly and give many infusions. Roasted Dong Ding takes water from about 95°C to a full boil. Aged oolong takes very hot water, in a pot that holds its heat, clay above all. Oriental Beauty is the exception and takes cooler water, about 80 to 95°C.

notice.text: A smooth, mellow, thick cup with little astringency, often plum or prune, sometimes something like medicinal herbs or ginseng, and an amber to red-brown liquor.
